identity.title: LER 2023-001-00 for Turkey Point Unit 3, RCS Pressure Boundary Degraded

cause.proximate_text: The most likely cause of the through-wall crack is intergranular stress-corrosion cracking (IGSCC). For IGSCC to occur, the following factors must be present: susceptible material, environment, and stress. The pressure stresses due to RCS pressure and the stress intensification of the geometry (i.e. the shoulder) contributed to the crack propagation. Additionally, the observed cracks and deterioration occurred in a sensitized region of the tube material, making it more susceptible to IGSCC.
cause.theme: Intergranular stress-corrosion cracking of sensitized guide tube material

chain: sensitized guide tube material + pressure/geometric stress -> intergranular stress-corrosion cracking (IGSCC) -> through-wall crack in Flux Mapper Seal Table Guide Tube H-6 -> RCS pressure boundary degraded / non-compliant with ASME Section XI standards
notes: Cause code is officially TBD/provisional per FORM-366; narrative attributes the crack to IGSCC driven by sensitized material, pressure stress, and geometric stress intensification, modeled as parallel contributing failure modes converging on the IGSCC mechanism. No SSFF occurred; event was low safety significance with no system actuation. No similar prior occurrences were identified in a 10-year review, so no SIMILAR_TO edge or stub LER was created.
